title: System Design: Learn the Connected Ideas
description: A 12-week teacher-guided sequence. Each week pairs a core system-design topic with the prerequisite knowledge that makes design decisions meaningful.

sessionFormat: Learn one concept from a video or article (45–60 min).
Explain it in your own words and draw the request/data flow (20 min).
Apply it to a small design prompt and state one trade-off (30–45 min).
Review with one failure scenario: traffic spike, node failure, stale data, or slow dependency (20 min).

weeks.outcome: Trace a browser request from URL entry to a response and estimate its bottleneck.
weeks.practice: Design the request path for a simple read-only profile page.

weeks.outcome: Turn vague requirements into numbers before choosing components.
weeks.practice: Estimate 10 million daily users uploading one 2 MB photo each.

weeks.outcome: Choose a load-balancing strategy and explain why application instances should usually be stateless.
weeks.practice: Scale a URL-shortener read API from one server to many.

weeks.outcome: Pick a storage model from access patterns instead of brand names.
weeks.practice: Model users, posts, follows, and a timeline query for a social app.

weeks.outcome: Place a cache safely and describe what happens on a miss, expiry, and outage.
weeks.practice: Design a product-details cache with a stale-data policy.

weeks.outcome: Choose a partition key and identify its uneven-load risks.
weeks.practice: Shard a multi-tenant message store by tenant and conversation.

weeks.outcome: State the consistency a feature needs and its user-visible compromise.
weeks.practice: Design a read-replica strategy for inventory without overselling.

weeks.outcome: Move slow work off the request path while keeping retries safe.
weeks.practice: Design image processing after a user uploads a photo.

weeks.outcome: Prevent one slow dependency from causing a cascading failure.
weeks.practice: Protect a payment checkout flow when the payment provider is slow.

weeks.outcome: Define how you will detect, diagnose, and measure a bad user experience.
weeks.practice: Specify dashboards and alerts for a notification service.

weeks.outcome: Design an API that is safe, evolvable, and realistic under retries.
weeks.practice: Draft create-payment and get-payment endpoints with error behavior.

weeks.outcome: Lead a structured 45-minute system-design answer without jumping prematurely into tools.
weeks.practice: Design one of: URL shortener, news feed, chat service, video platform, or ride matching.

interviewAnswerFramework: Clarify users, core actions, scale, latency, and consistency expectations.
Estimate traffic, storage, and peak load.
Draw the simplest end-to-end design first.
Deep dive into the one or two components that become bottlenecks.
Name trade-offs, failure modes, and observability before closing.
avoid: Memorizing diagrams without explaining the workload that requires each component.
Using microservices, Kafka, sharding, or Redis by default rather than from a stated need.
Ignoring data consistency, retries, and failure behavior.
